chapter.v:
These are
more proverbs of Solomon, collected by the scribes of Hezekiah, king of Judah.

God's greatness
is in doing things that can't be known, while the greatness of kings is in revealing things.

Just as
the height of the heavens or the depth of the earth can't be known, the king's thinking can't be known.

Remove the
waste from the silver, and the silversmith has pure silver to work with.

Remove the
wicked from the king's presence and the king will rule securely and justly.

Don't try
to make yourself look great before the king, and don't pretend to be among the important people,

for it's
better to be told, “Come up here,” than to be humiliated before a nobleman. Even though you've seen something with your own eyes,

don't rush
to take legal action, for what are you going to do in the end when your neighbor shows you're wrong and humiliates you?

Discuss the
case with your neighbor himself, and don't betray someone else's secret,

otherwise whoever
hears it will make you ashamed and you'll never lose your bad reputation.

Advice given
at the right time is like golden apples set in silver.

Constructive criticism
from the wise to someone who listens is like a gold ring and a necklace of fine gold.

Faithful messengers
are as refreshing to their master as cold snow on a hot harvest day.

Someone who
boasts about a gift they never give is like cloud and wind without rain.

If you're
patient you can persuade your superior, and soft words can break down opposition.

If you
find honey, eat just enough, for if you eat too much, you'll be sick.

Don't set
foot in your neighbors' homes too often, otherwise they'll get fed up with you and hate you.

Telling lies
in court against a friend is like attacking them with a mace, or a sword, or an arrow.

Trusting in
unreliable people in times of trouble is like eating with a broken tooth or walking on a bad foot.

Singing happy
songs to someone who's broken-hearted is like taking off your coat on a cold day, or pouring vinegar onto an open wound.

If your
enemy is hungry, give him something to eat; if he's thirsty, give him a drink of water.

This will
make him ashamed as if he had burning coals piled on his head, and the Lord will reward you.

In the
same way that the north wind brings rain, slandering people makes them angry.

It's better
to live in a corner of a housetop than to share a whole house with an argumentative wife.

Good news
from a distant country is like cold water to an exhausted traveler.

Good people
who give in to the wicked are like a muddied spring or a polluted well.

It's not
good to eat too much honey, or to want too much praise.

Someone without
control is as exposed as a town whose walls have been breached.
